definitions.explanation: A positive feeling or impression toward someone or something. Often used to describe the initial positive reaction people have toward a person, brand, or behavior.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}に{好感|こうかん}を{持|も}った。
examples.english: I took a liking to him.

examples.japanese: {誠実|せいじつ}な{態度|たいど}が{好感|こうかん}を{持|も}たれる。
examples.english: A sincere attitude earns a favorable impression.

examples.japanese: あの{芸能人|げいのうじん}は{好感度|こうかんど}ランキングで{常|つね}に{上位|じょうい}にいる。
examples.english: That celebrity is always near the top of the likability rankings.

notes:
USAGE:
The most common patterns are {好感|こうかん}を{持|も}つ (to have a favorable feeling toward) and {好感|こうかん}が{持|も}てる (to be able to feel favorable toward). The compound {好感度|こうかんど} (likability rating) is widely used in media.
Do not confuse with the homophone {交換|こうかん} (exchange).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {好感|こうかん}を{持|も}つ (to feel favorably toward)
- {好感|こうかん}が{持|も}てる (to find likable)
- {好感|こうかん}を{抱|いだ}く (to harbor a favorable feeling — more formal)
- {好感度|こうかんど} (likability; favorability rating)
- {好感度|こうかんど}が{高|たか}い (to have high likability)
